title: Red poppy
author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
paragraphs: The Red poppy (Papaver rhoeas), also known as the corn poppy, field poppy, common poppy, Flanders poppy, and Odai, is a species of flowering plant in the family Papaveraceae.  It is native to north Africa and temperate Eurasia.
The red poppy was first formally described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753. It has two subspecies and one variety.
The red poppy is native to north Africa and temperate Eurasia, but has been introduced to temperate areas worldwide. It grows on fields, beside roads, and on grasslands.

There is a variety of this plant, known as the Shirley poppy, that is commonly grown in gardens. It has edible seeds that can be eaten on their own or as an ingredient in bread, but most poppy seeds are harvested from the closely related opium poppy.
The petals contain a red dye found in some medicines and wines.
The petals were historically used to make a syrup that was used to help children sleep.
